title: Frog embryo brain gene expression is driven by voltage differences, not absolute values

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Frog embryo brain gene expression is driven by voltage differences, not absolute values

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the frog embryo brain, downstream gene expression is driven by the spatial difference in membrane voltage between regions rather than the absolute voltage of any cells, so cells must read patterns over whole cell fields: collectivity appears in the input as well as the output of cell-group behaviour.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Conclusion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For example, in the frog embryo brain, it is the spatial difference in voltage between regions that drives downstream gene expression, not the absolute value of any cells186,187.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Conclusion”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryonic brain patterning

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The competing predictors make the claim cleanly testable. Existing Xenopus resources cover expression and phenotypes, but paired spatial electrophysiology and transcript readouts needed for the decisive comparison are probably incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Model downstream brain-gene expression against absolute regional membrane voltage and against between-region voltage differences under perturbations that separate the two predictors. A cross-validated advantage for voltage differences supports the claim; equal or better prediction by absolute voltage refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Existing perturbations may confound voltage level and voltage contrast.

Public records may not pair spatial voltage maps with expression in the same embryos.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.85
data existence: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decision criterion is a standard physiological contrast, so the claim is operational. The experiments that report it do not have deposited paired voltage maps and spatial expression matrices, and bulk depolarization profiles cannot separate a difference code from an absolute-voltage code. Checking the claim as stated requires those paired measurements, which are not publicly analyzable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the Xenopus neural plate, record regional membrane voltage and the same embryos' brain-marker expression under two perturbations: one that changes absolute voltage while preserving the spatial contrast, and one that flattens the contrast. Expression should track the contrast if the claim is right, and absolute voltage if it is wrong.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public frog transcriptomes after depolarization do not include a matched arm that holds the spatial voltage difference constant.

The contrast-versus-absolute design has not been independently replicated with open raw files.

Voltage images and regional in situ results remain in the original papers rather than a public deposit.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.3
data existence: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.55
